name: iris scan hook with locking reticle
looks: A close macro of an eye fills the frame, grain and dot texture over the iris. A thin white bracket targets a point on it and tightens as the camera pushes in; a small HUD panel beside it starts as garbled characters, then the bracket turns violet and the panel resolves into a real status word with a latency number and a measurement.
build: A macro texture plate under a DOM bracket reticle pinned to the target, its corner gap narrowing on power2.out as the plate scales up for the push-in. The label text scrambles per frame then locks letter by letter (the end-card-decode mechanic); the readout ticks with no easing (the live-readout-hud mechanic). The bracket's stroke colour shifts from white to violet across the push-in.
sound: A low tonal hum under the push-in, a soft electronic chirp as the bracket locks, a couple of data ticks as the readout updates.
prompt: Open tight on a macro, textured close-up of a living or organic subject with a thin bracket reticle that locks onto one point and tightens as the camera pushes in. Run a small status label beside it through a quick character scramble before it locks to a real word, with a live measurement ticking under it, so the opening feels like the brand is actively sensing its subject rather than just showing it.
